summary: HTTP/2 HPACK decode failures and intermittent model-shard checksum errors behind customer NGFW due to TCP reassembly modification
description: Issue summary: Customers on a private deployment report intermittent model shard checksum failures and 502/GRPC errors during artifact downloads. Impact: Repeated shard re-downloads, model load failures causing increased latency and token cost for affected customers; BrightVista experiencing request error rates ~7% for model pulls in us-west-2.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy private agent in BrightVista VPC with corporate NGFW in egress path
Trigger a model cold-start that requires full shard range downloads (open-gpt-3b-quant)
Observe some artifact range fetches fail with HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR or RST_STREAM and later checksum mismatch reported by runtime
Capture packet trace from host and from egress NGFW span for failing request window
observed_behavior: Artifact fetch attempts intermittently fail with HTTP/2 PROTOCOL_ERROR (HPACK decode error) and gRPC code=13. Later the serving node reports SHA256 checksum mismatch for a shard range and retries the download, causing 5–15s stall and extra egress bandwidth.
expected_behavior: Artifact range fetches should complete without HTTP/2 protocol errors and checksums should match on first successful download; runtime should not need repeated retries due to wire reassembly issues.
logs_and_artifacts: serving-runtime logs: node-24/artifact-fetch ERROR 2026-03-09T14:22:13 - HPACK decode failure on stream 5
runtime checksum log: node-24/artifact-verify WARN shard-002 mismatch expected=3a7b... got=2f4c...
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports intermittent 502s + checksum mismatches during model cold starts. They only see the problem from their office network that routes egress through an NGFW vendor appliance.
BrightVista SRE (customer): We ran tcpdump and see out-of-order segments; our NGFW also shows packet modify/drop metrics. Happy to share captures.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): Captured both host and NGFW traces. Initial differential shows the NGFW reassembling and rewriting a TCP segment boundary — HPACK header block got split and a byte changed, causing decoder state mismatch.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): Proposed immediate workaround: add egress allowlist for artifact S3 hostnames via VPC endpoint or bypass NGFW for artifact traffic. Also advised disable TSO/GRO on hosts to reduce reassembly at middlebox.
BrightVista SRE: Confirmed that bypassing the appliance for artifact endpoints reduced error rate to <0.1% over 12h. Will work with NGFW vendor for permanent fix.
Support (Maya): Creating runbook entry and notifying Solutions Engineering to add private-deploy checklist for NGFW egress passthrough and host network offload recommendations.
investigation_notes: Packet analysis: host-side pcap shows HTTP/2 HEADERS (length ~1100 bytes) split across two TCP segments. NGFW-side pcap shows those segments merged then a single byte at offset 42 changed (likely normalization) before forwarding — HPACK compressed header block corrupted.

HTTP/2 decoder on runtime throws HPACK decoding error and responds with RST_STREAM/PROTOCOL_ERROR; client-side (artifact proxy) treats as transient and retries, but subsequent range is downloaded partially and verification fails due to mismatched bytes.
Reproducibility: Only reproducible when NGFW is in the path and TCP segmentation offload is enabled on host NICs. When TSO/GRO disabled, packet boundary changes stop and issue not reproducible.

Hypothesis: NGFW performs TCP reassembly/normalization and rewrites occasional bytes (hostname normalization, header inspection). Because HTTP/2 uses header compression state, mid-stream byte edits break HPACK state machine leading to PROTOCOL_ERROR instead of recoverable header mismatch. This then leads to partially corrupted range data being accepted until checksum verification triggers.
Short-term mitigation validated: Bypassing NGFW for artifact-host endpoints OR disabling NIC offloads prevents the reassembly path that triggers the NGFW rewrite.
Long-term: Customer vendor to apply a firmware/NGFW config to avoid reassembling/modifying HTTP/2 payloads or to offer an exception for artifact hosts.
workaround: 1) Configure VPC endpoint (VPCE) to fetch artifacts directly from S3 and exclude NGFW from that path, OR 2) On serving hosts disable TSO/GRO/LRO (ethtool settings) to avoid creating segment patterns that the NGFW rewrites. Both approaches validated by customer.
resolution: Partial - Provided validated workaround and runbook updates. Customer implemented VPCE allowlist for artifact S3 hostnames which eliminated failures. Engineering added a defensive retry/verify step in artifact-fetch: if HPACK/PROTOCOL_ERROR observed, runtime will fallback to smaller range sizes with fresh TCP connections and strict checksum verification. Permanent fix assigned to BrightVista and NGFW vendor to stop in-path HTTP/2 payload modification. Follow-up: Solutions Engineering to add 'NGFW HTTP/2 passthrough' checklist to private-deploy onboarding.
postmortem_followup_actions: SE-1273: Add 'NGFW egress passthrough' checklist to private deployment onboarding docs (Owners: Solutions Eng)
OPS-834: Add host NIC offload guidance to private-deploy runbook (Owners: Infra)
